name: ticket-manager
description: A compact issue and board sidebar for VS Code with Jira Cloud, demo, and file-backed modes.

ticketManager.backendMode.description: Choose whether the app uses Jira Cloud, Demo, GitHub, GitLab, Live Folder, or User Workspace mode.

ticketManager.connectionType.description: Legacy Jira MCP transport selector retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.connections.description: Named backend connections. Each entry is one configured backend instance (Jira server, GitLab host, Live Folder root, etc.). Use the Ticket Manager: Connections command to manage these via the UI.

id.description: Stable identifier for this connection. Used to reference it from tracked boards and secrets.

settings.description: Mode-specific settings (URL, project key, MCP command, folder path, etc.). Secrets are stored separately in VS Code SecretStorage.

ticketManager.boards.description: Boards the user has explicitly chosen to track. Each entry references a connection by id and a board id native to that backend.

connectionId.description: Id of the connection this board belongs to (must match an entry in ticketManager.connections).

displayName.description: Optional override for the board's display name in the sidebar.

ticketManager.jiraCloudBaseUrl.description: Base URL used by the built-in Jira polling and delivery runtime in Jira Cloud mode.

ticketManager.jiraCloudToken.description: Bearer token used by the built-in Jira polling and delivery runtime in Jira Cloud mode. If empty, Ticket Manager falls back to JIRA_TOKEN.

ticketManager.jiraCloudEpicKey.description: Optional Jira Epic key associated with this workspace in Jira Cloud mode. Boards and polling sync follow this epic, and Jira issue creation uses it as the default parent epic.

ticketManager.jiraCloudEpicBoardName.description: Optional display name for the Jira Cloud epic board in this workspace.

ticketManager.jiraCloudBoardJql.description: Optional Jira JQL query associated with this workspace in Jira Cloud mode. When set, a JQL board is shown in addition to any linked epic board.

ticketManager.jiraCloudBoardName.description: Optional display name for the Jira Cloud JQL board in this workspace.

ticketManager.jiraOAuthClientId.description: Client ID of the Atlassian OAuth 2.0 app used to connect Jira Cloud.

ticketManager.jiraOAuthScopes.description: OAuth scopes requested when connecting Jira Cloud. Defaults to offline_access, read:jira-work, write:jira-work, read:jira-user, read:me, read:board-scope:jira-software, read:project:jira, and read:issue-details:jira.

ticketManager.jiraCloudId.description: Atlassian Cloud ID of the connected Jira Cloud site. Set automatically after a successful OAuth connection.

ticketManager.jiraCloudSiteName.description: Display name of the connected Jira Cloud site. Set automatically after a successful OAuth connection.

ticketManager.jiraCloudSiteUrl.description: URL of the connected Jira Cloud site. Set automatically after a successful OAuth connection.

ticketManager.enableCreateIdea.markdownDescription: Enable the **Create Idea** command and button (preview). When disabled, the command and its icon are hidden.

ticketManager.enableNewProject.markdownDescription: Enable the **New Project** wizard (preview). When disabled, the command is hidden from the Command Palette.

ticketManager.boardsSidebarPreviewMode.markdownDescription: Select the **Boards** sidebar layout. **Classic** uses separate views (Boards, EPICs, My Issues, Sessions, Issue Details). **Work Mode** uses a board-centric layout with boards as cards and nested agent sessions.

ticketManager.githubPat.description: GitHub Personal Access Token for authenticating with the GitHub API.

ticketManager.githubUrl.description: GitHub API base URL. Use the default for github.com or set to your GitHub Enterprise Server URL (e.g. https://github.example.com/api/v3).

ticketManager.githubOwner.description: GitHub organisation or user that owns the repositories to manage.

ticketManager.gitlabUrl.description: GitLab instance URL (e.g. https://gitlab.com or https://gitlab.example.com).

ticketManager.gitlabApiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: **Deprecated**: The GitLab API key is now stored securely in the OS keychain via VS Code SecretStorage. This setting is read once on startup for migration and then cleared automatically. Use the Setup panel to re-enter your key.
ticketManager.gitlabApiKey.description: Deprecated. GitLab Personal Access Token — migrated to SecretStorage on first load.

ticketManager.requestTimeoutMs.description: Timeout, in milliseconds, for MCP requests.

ticketManager.defaultPageSize.description: Number of issues to request per page.

ticketManager.jiraPolling.enabled.markdownDescription: Start the built-in Node.js Jira poller when the extension activates in **Jira via MCP** or **Jira Cloud** mode. Disabled by default (opt-in). Polling activity is logged to the **Ticket Manager** output channel, and the first successful poll shows a confirmation notification.

ticketManager.jiraPolling.requiredLabel.markdownDescription: Jira label used as the AI execution gate by the built-in poller. In **Jira Cloud** mode, linked-epic tasks are synced regardless of label, but only tasks with this label are eligible for AI execution.

ticketManager.jiraPolling.clarificationA.markdownDescription: When enabled, the poller runs a readiness analysis on each eligible ticket and may post clarification questions before starting work. When disabled (default), the agent proceeds directly to implementation with the information available on the ticket.

ticketManager.delivery.defaultBaseBranch.markdownDescription: Default base branch to use when a Jira ticket does not specify one (e.g. `main`, `develop`). When empty, the agent will post a clarification comment asking for the branch.

ticketManager.delivery.autoMergeSubTasks.markdownDescription: When enabled (default), completed sub-task branches are automatically merged into the feature branch without creating a merge request. A single MR is raised from the feature branch to the base branch after all sub-tasks complete. When disabled, each sub-task creates its own MR targeting the feature branch.

ticketManager.workspaceMcpServerName.description: Optional workspace MCP server name to use from .vscode/mcp.json when Jira via MCP mode is not manually configured.

ticketManager.userMcpServerRef.description: Optional user/profile MCP server reference to use when Jira via MCP mode is not manually configured and no workspace MCP server is selected.

ticketManager.priorityColors.description: Colors for the priority indicator bar on ticket cards. Values can be hex colors or CSS linear gradients.

ticketManager.jiraBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon to the left of each board name in the Boards list when a **Jira** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#3b82f6`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.demoBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **Demo** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#a855f7`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.fileBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **File** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#22c55e`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.liveFolderPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a `plans` folder, `features` folder, or parent folder to search for `features/feature-NN-*/feature.md` and `story-*.md` files. Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderProjectKey.markdownDescription: Project key for issues derived from the live folder (e.g. `EXAMPLE`). Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderProjectName.markdownDescription: Human-readable project name for the live folder (e.g. `ExampleHIS Integration`). Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderAllowIssueCreati.markdownDescription: Allow Ticket Manager to create new markdown issue files when **Live Folder** mode is active. Disable this to keep the live folder read-only from the extension.

ticketManager.liveFolderBoardListIconCol.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **Live Folder** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#f59e0b`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.ai.openaiApiKey.description: OpenAI API key for AI agent assignment.

ticketManager.ai.claudeApiKey.description: Claude/Anthropic API key for AI agent assignment.

ticketManager.ai.cursorCliPath.description: Path to the Cursor CLI executable for AI agent assignment.

ticketManager.ai.copilotEnabled.description: Enable the GitHub Copilot SDK for AI reviews, in-app @copilot comment replies, and Copilot agent tasks.

ticketManager.ai.copilotCliPath.description: Legacy compatibility override for the runtime used by the GitHub Copilot SDK. Leave empty unless you are debugging a local Copilot SDK installation.

ticketManager.ai.copilotAgentName.description: Display and @mention name for the GitHub Copilot agent. Leave empty to use the built-in GitHub Copilot SDK label.

ticketManager.ai.claudeCliPath.description: Path to the Claude Code CLI executable for AI agent assignment.

ticketManager.ai.defaultProvider.description: Default AI provider to use when assigning tickets to an AI agent.

ticketManager.ai.defaultModel.description: Default AI model to store on newly created live-folder markdown tickets when a model is configured. Leave empty to omit the model field.

ticketManager.ai.analysisEnabled.description: Enable the per-issue analysis gate before assigning a ticket to AI.

ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultPrompt.default:
# Technical Ticket Readiness Review Prompt

You are a senior technical analyst and reviewer with strong expertise across backend, frontend, infrastructure, integrations, data, APIs, CI/CD, and production systems.

Your task is to review a development ticket (e.g. Jira) and determine whether it is sufficiently defined for **safe, accurate implementation**.

Your review must be **practical, code-aware, version-aware, and implementation-focused**.

---

## Core Rules

- Analyse in a **step-by-step structure**, explicitly stating the step being performed
- Report **findings, gaps, and risks only** (no internal reasoning or chain-of-thought)
- Do **not invent missing details**
- Be precise, critical, and concise
- Focus on **implementation readiness, code impact, technology compatibility, and delivery risk**
- All guidance must be compatible with the **actual technologies and versions** used

---

## Mandatory Requirements

1. **Ticket review**
   - Title, description, acceptance criteria, comments, attachments, linked tickets

2. **Linked tickets**
   - Analyse each once only
   - Avoid duplicates
   - Detect circular references and stop safely

3. **Repository & artefact analysis**
   - Inspect referenced repos, services, files, designs, schemas
   - Identify likely impacted code areas

4. **Technology discovery & compatibility validation (MANDATORY)**
   - Identify languages, frameworks, runtimes, platforms, and versions
   - Unknown or unverifiable versions must be flagged as risks or blockers

5. **Code-level impact analysis (MANDATORY)**
   - Map requirements to specific code layers/components
   - Inability to map code impact = blocker

6. **Readiness rule**
   - A ticket is **not ready** if code impact or technology compatibility cannot be validated

---

## Required Review Steps

### STEP 1 — Ticket Understanding

**Task**
- Review the ticket and directly relevant linked items

**Findings**
- Problem being solved
- Expected outcome / deliverable
- Constraints, assumptions, dependencies
- Referenced teams, systems, services, environments, releases
- Acceptance criteria: existence and testability
- Explicit technology references

---

### STEP 2 — Linked Ticket Validation

**Task**
- Analyse each linked ticket once; detect circular references

**Findings**
- Linked tickets reviewed
- Relevant findings and dependencies
- Missing or inaccessible linked tickets

---

### STEP 3 — Repository & Artefact Validation

**Task**
- Identify and validate all referenced repos, services, designs, schemas, configs

**Findings**
- Available vs missing artefacts
- Why missing artefacts matter
- [Critical] flag if implementation context is missing

---

### STEP 4 — Technology Discovery & Compatibility Validation (MANDATORY)

**Task**
- Determine actual technology stack and validate implementation compatibility

**Identify**
- Languages, versions, frameworks, runtimes, SDKs, platforms, build tooling, package management, databases, infrastructure constraints

**Validation**
- Ensure suggestions fit discovered stack
- Flag version mismatches or unsupported patterns
- Distinguish: confirmed / inferred / unknown versions
- [Critical] flag if compatibility cannot be validated

---

### STEP 5 — Code Impact Analysis (MANDATORY)

**Task**
- Map requirements to likely code changes (compatible with discovered stack)

**Analyse across**
- API, business logic, domain, data access, database/schema, UI/frontend, integrations, config, infrastructure, logging, security, tests

**For each impacted area**
- Repo / service / module affected
- Change type (new feature, bug fix, enhancement, refactor, config, schema)
- Certain vs inferred impact
- Compatibility considerations
- [Critical] flag if code impact cannot be determined

---

### STEP 6 — Completeness Assessment

**Task**
- Assess whether ticket has sufficient detail for safe implementation

**Gap categories**
- Functional requirements (behaviours, rules, flows, acceptance conditions)
- Non-functional requirements (performance, security, reliability, observability)
- Data / contracts / interfaces (inputs, outputs, validation, schemas)
- Error handling / edge cases (failures, retries, idempotency, rollback)
- Dependencies (teams, systems, release sequencing)
- Technology compatibility (missing versions, unknown constraints)

**Label each gap**: [Critical] / [Major] / [Minor]

---

### STEP 7 — Technology & Domain Analysis

**Task**
- Summarise all relevant technologies and domain concepts

**Findings**
- Key technologies and versions
- Ambiguous technical/domain concepts
- Risks from unclear architecture, integrations, legacy constraints, security, compliance
- Concise stack summary (e.g. Backend: .NET 4.8 C# 7.3, Frontend: jQuery, DB: SQL Server)

---

### STEP 8 — Implementation View

**Task**
- Describe likely implementation approach at high level

**Findings**
- Strategy, code paths, key decisions, trade-offs
- Cross-cutting concerns
- Technology constraints shaping approach
- Testing and rollout implications

---

### STEP 9 — Risk Assessment

**Categories**: requirement ambiguity, technical complexity, code impact uncertainty, technology compatibility, integration/dependency, delivery, operational, maintainability, testability

**For each risk**: title, severity (Low/Medium/High), explanation, justification

---

### STEP 10 — Readiness Evaluation

- **Completeness score**: 0–100%
- **Confidence level**: Low / Medium / High
- **Justification** based on analysis evidence

---

### STEP 11 — Final Decision

Choose ONE:
- ✅ Ready to implement
- ⚠️ Implementable with clarifications
- ❌ Not ready for implementation

Rule: if technology compatibility cannot be validated → not ✅

---

### STEP 12 — Prioritised Next Actions

Specific, actionable, implementation-focused actions in priority order.

---

## Output Rules

- Use exact step headings (STEP 1–12)
- Concise bullet points
- Distinguish: confirmed / inferred / missing information
- No internal reasoning or chain-of-thought
- Do not invent details
- State clearly if implementation cannot proceed safely
ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultPrompt.description: Required default prompt used in the Analysis Window. If empty, analysis gating is treated as disabled at runtime.

ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultModel.description: Default model used by the Analysis Window. Leave empty to fall back to ticketManager.ai.defaultModel.

ticketManager.ai.openaiAgentName.description: Display name for the OpenAI agent (e.g. 'GPT-4 Reviewer'). When set, this name appears as an assignee option and is used when assigning tickets to the OpenAI agent.

ticketManager.ai.claudeAgentName.description: Display name for the Claude agent (e.g. 'Claude AI'). When set, this name appears as an assignee option and is used when assigning tickets to the Claude agent.

ticketManager.ai.verboseActivityFeed.description: Show all event types (tool calls, permission requests, etc.) in the AI session activity feed. When disabled, only high-value events like messages, plans, and errors are shown.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryWorkflowEnabled.description: When enabled, Jira polling moves implementation-ready issues into the delivery workflow instead of posting the full Copilot conversation back into Jira comments.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryPublishCommand.description: Repository-specific command the Copilot delivery workflow must run inside the dedicated worktree to publish the MSI artifact.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryArtifactPattern.description: Glob or relative path pattern, from the delivery worktree root, that identifies the MSI artifact(s) to attach back to Jira.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryAgentWorkflowPa.description: Optional repo-relative or absolute path to the workflow-pack skill folder or SKILL.md file that Copilot must follow for Jira delivery tasks. Example: .github/skills/add-edit-dotnet-web-api

ticketManager.ai.deliveryAgentWorkflowUr.description: Optional GitLab or web URL for the assigned delivery workflow pack. When set, the Jira start comment includes this link.

ticketManager.ai.deliverySummaryTemplate.description: Optional Jira summary comment template. Supported placeholders: {{summary}}, {{branch}}, {{commitHash}}, {{pushedRef}}, {{artifactNames}}.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryFailureTemplate.description: Optional Jira failure comment template. Supported placeholders: {{failureReason}}, {{branch}}, {{commitHash}}, {{pushedRef}}.
